F1_ledger_15_overdue.reported: forecast population live_forward: 15 forecast(s) past due and unresolved
F1_ledger_15_overdue.verdict: FALSE POSITIVE - a measurement artefact, not a resolver failure
F1_ledger_15_overdue.root_cause: ledger_health counted overdue on `today >= resolves_after`, the same predicate resolve_due uses to pick what to GRADE. The resolver is a 16:30 ET cron (20:30 UTC); the canary is a clock. Every record maturing on date D reads as past due from 00:00 UTC on D until the resolver's slot at 20:30 UTC - 20.5 of every 24 hours.

the_15.identification: precisely the live_forward records whose resolves_after == 2026-09-03
the_15.why_not: no read-only prod surface names ACTIONABLE overdue records - the health row carried a bare integer while naming the QUARANTINED ids. Fixed in commit 2908a06 (ledger_health now emits `overdue_actionable`); the ids become readable on the next deploy.
the_15.derivation: the ledger file did not change between the two observations: n_records 237, n_resolved 42, n_void 6, last_written 2026-09-02 in both. Only `today` advanced. n_overdue went 25 -> 40; 40 - 25 = 15 crossed the threshold at 00:00 UTC on 2026-09-03, so all 15 have resolves_after == 2026-09-03.

F2_nav_not_fresh.reported: nav not fresh - all 10 lanes last_nav_date 2026-09-01, expected 2026-09-02, last_mtm ran 2026-09-02T23:30
F2_nav_not_fresh.verdict: REAL FAULT, structural and chronic - repaired in data and in code
F2_nav_not_fresh.root_cause: _get_current_prices and _get_latest_bar_date both set end = datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d'). yfinance's `end` is EXCLUSIVE, so the newest bar either can return is YESTERDAY'S. mark_lane_to_market stamps the NAV row with that bar's date (P-day-2026-08-19a), so every close mark landed on the PREVIOUS session - the exact outcome that change set out to prevent.
F2_nav_not_fresh.why_it_looked_green: mark_lane_to_market returned a float for all 10 lanes, so the MTM receipt read status marked, n_marked 10, n_failed 0. The receipt PRINTS expected_nav_date but never compares the written row against it, so it cannot detect the fault it exists to detect.
F2_nav_not_fresh.duty_cycle: _expected_nav_date rolls to today at 17:00 ET while the mark writes D-1, so nav.all_fresh could only be true between the 16:30 mark and 17:00 ET - about 30 minutes a day.

data_repair.doubles_as_proof: running the UNMODIFIED job one calendar day later produced the 2026-09-02 bar. Same code, same lanes; the fetch window was the only variable.

F2_nav_not_fresh.deploy_caveat: post-fix the 16:30 mark writes D instead of D-1, so D-1 must already be marked or it is skipped permanently. Trigger pi_hourly_mtm on the CURRENT code before deploying. Done for 2026-09-02 by this pass.
F2_nav_not_fresh.data_loss: none - no session row was lost

F4_why_moved_crash.verdict: REAL crash - but AFTER the job had completed all of its work. Repaired.
F4_why_moved_crash.root_cause: scheduler.py:1314 summed l.get('rejections') over result['lenses'], which run_why_moved returns as a DICT keyed by lens name. Iterating it bare yields lens NAMES (str).

F4_why_moved_crash.test_gap: 9 tests cover this job; every fake returned lenses: [] so none ever saw the real shape, while test_why_moved.py asserted out['lenses']['options_vol'] on the producer side
F4_why_moved_crash.second_route_same_error: why_moved._extract_json is annotated -> dict but is json.loads, which returns str for a JSON string literal and list for an array. Those parse cleanly, bypass the JSONDecodeError guard and reach parse_hypotheses' raw.get(). Double-encoded JSON is a known DeepSeek json_object failure mode. Also fixed.
